request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Changing a plan's amount now also changes the amount of the claims it generated that are still
DRAFT (each as the claim form would edit it, writing CLAIM_EDITED); claims in any other status keep
theirs.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Changing a plan's amount now also updates the claims that plan generated which are still DRAFT. Each one is written to the audit file as `CLAIM_EDITED`, right after the `PLAN_CHANGED` line. Claims in any other status keep their old amount. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed:**
- **Server:** a new step, `claim/EditPlanDrafts.java`, runs after the plan's amount is changed. It goes through the claims the plan generated, oldest first, and gives each DRAFT the new amount. It records you as the last editor, saves it, and writes `CLAIM_EDITED` in the same format the claim editor uses. `PlanRepository` has a new `madeClaims(planId)` method that lists those claims.
- **Endpoint:** `plans/{planId}/amount.POST.yml` now runs this step. I also gave it the same before/after rollup lines the claim editor has, so if a draft edit ever moves a total, it's recorded. In the tests no totals moved, so no extra lines were written.
- **Front end:** after saving a plan amount, the screen now re-reads the whole sheet instead of just the plans. Without this, the edited drafts would only show their new amount after a reload. Generate already works this way.

**Choices I made that the request didn't settle:**
- **Drafts the claim editor would refuse are skipped, not refused.** That covers a draft whose editor another user has open, one due inside a closed period, and one whose line items add up to a different amount. Those drafts keep their old amount and the plan change still goes through. The alternative is to refuse the whole plan change when any draft can't be edited; tell me if you'd rather have that.
- **A draft that already has the new amount is left alone,** so no `CLAIM_EDITED` line is written for it. The claim editor itself writes that line even when nothing changed.
- **Plans that send their claims to a descendant sheet** have their drafts edited on that sheet. The audit lines and any total changes go to that sheet's audit, as generate already does. The tests don't cover this case.
